newsitem.title: USA: AA sees early start to Q4 air cargo peak.
newsitem.headline: AA sees early start to Q4 air cargo peak.

text.p: American Airlines has seen an especially early start to the pre-Christmas air freight peak, says Mark Najarian, vice-president of U.S. cargo sales.
"We had a good September and the first 15-16 days of October were much better than we had forecast," he said told Reuters.
Yields are up, but especially volume, he said.
U.S.-Latin American traffic continues to run almost 30 percent head of year-ago levels.
American's freight loads out of Japan "are doing much, much, much, much better than we were doing a year ago or 6-7 months ago," he said.
"It's not like (ex-Japan) is doing better three days out of the week - it is doing better every day of the week," he said.
In certain acute demand corridors, American is either raising rates or opting to carry only higher-yielding traffic.
This week, the carrier implemented a five percent cargo rate increase on traffic to the U.S. from Central America, he said.
American also is implementing some individual account increases with large customers, he said.
Europe is doing fine in both directions, even though American has less North Atlantic cargo capacity than in 1995, he said.
Yet, Najarian said he is taking a cautious view towards the balance of the pre-Christmas period.
"It's a little unnerving that we are seeing so much volume this early in October," he said. "As good as it is, and as much as we like it, it's unusual."
"I hope we don't get to November and all of a sudden it dies." -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
